text:
jess: Heads-up — on the long-context perf harness (1M tokens session) we saw steady KV cache RSS growth on hosted. Dedicated run with same model+config stayed flat. Anyone seen this pattern before?
rohan: Can you paste the memory profile + jemalloc stats and the exact config used? kernel/glibc versions matter here.
mikaela: quick summary from my side: I ran perf + heaptrack on the failing hosted instance. Short notes: a) lots of tiny allocations during KV compaction path, b) increasing number of anonymous mmaps, c) smaps shows resident rising from ~4G -> ~11G over the session.
infra-bot: alert: kv-residency-growth firing on hosted-staging-443 (kv_rss > 8GB sustained) 2023-03-10T14:22Z
sam: hypothesis — config drift between hosted and dedicated. Dedicated nodes have jemalloc pinned + THP disabled. Hosted might be on a newer glibc/kernel and THP=always causing fragmentation. Also private/onprem had similar symptoms after GPU OOMs (slab fragmentation).
jin: also note we changed remap fallback in runtime 0.12.2; it uses mremap to expand internal buffers which can leave holes until compaction. Could be more visible on hosted due to different ASLR / allocator defaults.
jess: repro command I'm using locally:
```
# reproduce long-context growth
./bin/inference --model redwood-13b --long-context --kv-evict-threshold=0.7 --trace-kv --profile-interval=100000
# collect smaps every 100k tokens
while true; do pid=$(pgrep -f "inference --model"); cat /proc/$pid/smaps > /tmp/smaps.$(date +%s); sleep 60; done &
```
rohan: can you attach the jemalloc stats (mallctl) output and the exact kernel, glibc, and jemalloc package versions for both hosted and dedicated?
mikaela: attached snippet from hosted run (trimmed):
```
RSS: 4.1G -> 11.2G over 1,000,000 tokens
page_faults: minor=124k major=12
anon_mapped: 9.6G
jemalloc: allocated=8.3G resident=11.0G fragmentation>20% (small bins hot)
mmap_count: 7.2k
```
sam: on dedicated the same run shows:
```
RSS: 4.0G -> 4.5G
mmap_count: 1.1k
jemalloc: allocated=8.1G resident=4.6G fragmentation<5%
```
jin: big delta in mmap_count is interesting. That suggests many short-lived mmaps or fallback allocations on hosted. Could be the allocator flags or a runtime fallback kernel path that maps pages instead of reusing frames.
jess: action idea — replicate dedicated environment on a hosted staging VM: pin jemalloc, match glibc, set THP=never, same kernel if possible. Run deterministic harness and record /proc/pid/smaps and jemalloc stats.
rohan: +1. Also open infra ticket to temporarily disable THP on one hosted host and run. If that removes growth, we know the compaction path is sensitive to THP.
mikaela: I'll schedule runs: 1) hosted-staging with jemalloc pinned, 2) hosted-staging with THP disabled, 3) dedicated baseline, 4) onprem replay (we need to capture slabinfo after GPU OOM). Collect perf, smaps, jemalloc stats, and mmap_count every 100k tokens.
sam: small note — VPC/networking differences (MTU, NIC offloads) can affect hugepage alignment only in weird cases; I don't think that's primary but mention due to past incidents where driver affected cuMemMap alignment.
jess: good point — include driver/kernel build flags in comparison. I'll run the repro and upload logs to the infra ticket.
mikaela: I'll also add extra tracing in the runtime: dump kv-pageframe list sizes at compaction and emit a debug marker when we fall back to `mmap` path. That should correlate with the mmap_count spike.
rohan: plan: 1) repro runs (mikaela+jess) 2) infra disables THP on one host and pins jemalloc on another 3) collect traces and compare mmap_count + fragmentation metrics 4) if matched, either change allocation strategy or force compacting after remap.
jess: sounds good. Can someone spin up a dedicated-run replay for tomorrow 09:00 PT so we have a same-time comparison? @mikaela
mikaela: on it, calendar invite sent.
jess: thanks. Also adding a quick checklist in the infra ticket: kernel/glibc/jemalloc versions, THP setting, hugepages, driver versions, per-process smaps, jemalloc stats, mmap_count, perf samples.
sam: FYI — on private onprem we've seen KV reuse degrade after repeated GPU OOMs; add slabinfo and /proc/slabinfo dumps to the list for onprem runs.
jin: cool. if we find it's allocator config, we should make a defensive runtime change: prefer in-place compaction and avoid remap fallbacks when fragmentation > X.
jess: agreed. I'll update the ticket with the repro artifacts and next steps after first runs. :thumbsup:
